title: Ramp-and-Hold throughput suite for Dedicated capacity (micro-bursts overlay)
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable, telemetry-rich ramp-and-hold throughput test for Dedicated capacity that exercises autoscaler behavior under realistic interleaved steady-state + micro-burst traffic. This ticket owns the harness, detection rules for regressions in tokens/sec and p95 latency, and a short runbook for interpreting results. The suite is intended to catch both capacity regressions (reduced sustained tokens/sec) and latency regressions (p95 slip) caused by kernel changes, batching tuning, KV-cache regressions, or autoscaler configuration drift.

Scope: implement the harness driver, define traffic mix and stage profiles, wire metric collection (tokens/sec, p95, GPU util, queue length, KV cache hit rate), implement regression detector rules, and run baseline against current runtime-1.22 images and quantized model variants. Produce a baseline artifact (dashboard link + CSV summary) and open follow-up tickets for any regressions found.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness can run unattended for the full schedule and output per-window metrics (1s and 30s windows) for tokens/sec and latency p50/p95/p99.
2) Detectable regression rules implemented: (a) sustained tokens/sec drop >10% relative to baseline for 3 consecutive 60s windows; (b) p95 increase >15% relative to baseline for 3 consecutive 60s windows; (c) p95 absolute breach >350ms for any 60s window flagged as high-priority.
3) Test includes cold-cache, warm-cache ramp, steady hold, and micro-burst overlay phases.
4) Results written to S3 and linked dashboard; baseline CSV and run metadata checked in.
5) Alerts (Slack + ticket template) created when regression rules trigger.
6) Run produces annotated artifact with actionable triage pointers (likely subsystems: kernel selection, batching, KV cache).
implementation_notes:
Harness: extend existing ThroughputRunner (Go) with a new 'ramp_and_hold' profile. Key features: per-worker KV-cache warmup control, token-level synthetic prompts (short/medium/long shape mix), request pacing to target tokens/sec per-GPU, and micro-burst inserter.

Traffic profile:
- Cold-cache priming: 2 minutes at 10% target load using long requests to populate KV cache.
- Ramp-up: linear ramp from 10% to 85% target over 8 minutes.
- Hold: 20 minutes at 85% target sustained throughput.
- Micro-burst overlay: every 90s insert a 8s high-Intensity burst at +40% of target to simulate tenant spikes.
- Cooldown: 5 minutes at 20%

Request shapes (mix by request count): 50% short (8 tokens), 35% medium (128 tokens), 15% long (1k tokens). This yields token-distribution realistic for product usage.

Autoscaler knobs to exercise: scale-up threshold (GPU util >=85% OR queue-ms >=200ms sustained 60s), scale-down hysteresis (minimum 180s), max-scale-step, and headroom reservation for canary priority pools. Record decisions emitted by autoscaler in logs to correlate with observed latency regressions.

Metric plumbing: export to Prometheus using the job label 'ramp_and_hold/ENG-99412'. Additional span tags: run_id, model_variant, quantization, deployment_id. Persist raw per-request traces to S3 (sampled at 1%).
test_plan:
1) Baseline: run against runtime-1.22 + model-v2-fp16 (current gold). Capture metrics and mark as baseline.
2) Variant runs: runtime-1.22 + model-v2-4bit, runtime-1.23-canary + model-v2-fp16, runtime-1.23-canary + model-v2-4bit.
3) For each run capture: aggregate tokens/sec (1s/30s windows), p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU util, queue-ms distribution, KV cache hit rate, and autoscaler events.
4) Post-process: compute relative deltas against baseline and run regression detection rules.
5) Manual triage: for any rule-triggered runs, collect flamegraphs, kernel selection histograms, and batching distribution to attach to ticket.

Run cadence: daily for canary builds, weekly for release candidates, and ad-hoc for kernel/hotfix patches.
results_summary: (placeholder) First dry-run executed 2026-03-12 against runtime-1.22/model-v2-fp16. Observations: ramp and hold succeeded; micro-burst overlay caused transient p95 spikes but recovered within 30s. Baseline tokens/sec: 780k tokens/sec aggregated across pool (30s median). Baseline p95: 142ms during hold. No regression rules triggered for this dry-run. Next: run quantized variant and runtime-1.23 canary. Detailed CSV uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/ENG-99412/2026-03-12-run.csv. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/benchmarks/ramp-and-hold?orgId=1&var-run=ENG-99412-20260312
next_steps:
1) Schedule quantized model run (model-v2-4bit) and runtime-1.23 canary by 2026-03-16.
2) Add an autoscaler shadow run mode to emit hypothetical scale decisions (no actual scaling) to aid correlation when diagnosing regressions.
3) If regression detected, collect: per-GPU kernel histogram, batching distribution, and sample traces (attach to follow-up ticket).
4) Document runbook for on-call: how to interpret drop vs latency regressions and quick mitigations (rollback model variant, increase headroom, reduce batch target).
